1	# Coding manual r2 (frozen; coding-rule revision after Gate 1 — the THEORY is unchanged). Code each record independently, from its own text only.
2	
3	## A. Operations
4	For every performative act in a record (the headline and the Effect column), decide which operation it is **by the verb the record itself uses**, using this table.
5	- An act whose verb is not in the table is listed under `not_modelled`, using the record's own verb (e.g. "RENAME").
6	- If an act fits two rows of the table, use the headline's performative.
7	
8	| Operation | Verbs in the record |
9	|---|---|
10	| ADOPT | "adopted" said of a ruling that was PREPARED (awaiting adoption) |
11	| ADOPT-DECISION | "adopted"/"adoption" said of an option, path, rename, review or decision (first instance) |
12	| APPROVE | "approved", "approval" (a plan, realization, strategy or rule) |
13	| DEFER | "deferred", "deferral" |
14	| OPEN-WORK | "opened" (a work package) |
15	| RATIFY | "ratified" |
16	| DECLARE-SCOPE | "declared" of a scope or boundary |
17	| CONFIRM | "confirmed" (no change) |
18	| SEAL | "sealed" |
19	| REFINE-CANDIDATE | "candidate … refined" |
20	| MODIFY-SEQUENCE | "sequence modified" |
21	| AUTHORIZE | "authorized" |
22	| ACCEPT | "accepted" (completed work or a completed assessment) |
23	| SUBDIVIDE | "subdivided", "split" |
24	| WITHDRAW | "withdrawn" |
25	| HOLD | "held" |
26	| ANNOTATE | "annotated", "annotation", "redirect", "pointer" |
27	| DETERMINE | "determined", "classified" |
28	| RECLASSIFY | "reclassified" |
29	| FREEZE / LIFT | "frozen"/"freeze" / "lifted", "released" |
30	| REJECT | "not adopted", "rejected", "declined" |
31	| SUPERSEDE | "supersedes", "superseded by" |
32	| CREATE-NORM | a rule or discipline established ("shall", "is the rule", "discipline") |
33	| RAISE | "promoted" (raised to a higher standing) |
34	| ALLOCATE | "allocated" |
35	| PERMIT | "permitted", "permission" |
36	| CONTRA | counter-evidence recorded |
37	| CORRECT-TEXT | a same-day correction of the record's own text |
38	
39	## B. Each operation's frame (the only things it may change directly)
40	
41	| Operation | May change |
42	|---|---|
43	| ADOPT | status, annotation-role |
44	| ADOPT-DECISION | decision-in-force |
45	| APPROVE | approval of the target |
46	| DEFER | deferral of the target |
47	| OPEN-WORK | work lifecycle |
48	| RATIFY | standing of the target |
49	| DECLARE-SCOPE | scope norm |
50	| CONFIRM | nothing |
51	| SEAL | the document's regime |
52	| REFINE-CANDIDATE | candidate content |
53	| MODIFY-SEQUENCE | sequence |
54	| AUTHORIZE | authorization (scoped) |
55	| ACCEPT | acceptance, work lifecycle (acceptance may close work) |
56	| SUBDIVIDE | work structure |
57	| WITHDRAW / HOLD | status |
58	| ANNOTATE | annotation |
59	| DETERMINE / RECLASSIFY | classification, evidence status |
60	| FREEZE / LIFT | regime (scoped) |
61	| REJECT | nothing |
62	| SUPERSEDE | authoritative location (the old record kept) |
63	| CREATE-NORM | norm |
64	| RAISE | standing |
65	
66	**Consequences that follow automatically** (e.g. "X becomes acceptable", "queue item closed") are *derived*, not direct changes.
67	
68	## C. Legality guards (what makes an act permitted)
69	- **ADOPT** a PREPARED ruling: only by the Decision Authority, never by its own issuer.
70	- **START / execution:** only with full authorization (any stated precondition discharged). Permission alone never allows execution.
71	- **Evidence bars:**
72	  - RAISE needs ≥ 2 supporting instances or an exception;
73	  - SUPERSEDE needs sufficient evidence or a structural rule;
74	  - creating new vocabulary, categories or a methodology extension needs demonstrated need;
75	  - authorizing a successor slice needs the predecessor accepted;
76	  - reopening needs materially new evidence.
77	
78	## D. Code seven judgements per record
79	Values: SUPPORTED, VIOLATED, UNTESTABLE (does not apply), NOT-MODELLED (the relevant act is not in the table), AMBIGUOUS (the text allows two readings). For V6 on records numbered below R-43, use PRE-R43.
80	
81	| # | Judgement | Code SUPPORTED / VIOLATED when |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| V1 | Legality | every act the record performs is permitted by §C, and every refusal that cites a rule concerns an act §C forbids. VIOLATED if a performed act breaks §C, with the relevant facts stated in the record |
84	| V2 | Separation of permission / authorization / commissioning / execution | the record keeps them apart. VIOLATED if it treats one as the other without a separate act |
85	| V3 | Frames | every explicitly stated direct change fits §B for its operation. VIOLATED if a stated direct change falls outside |
86	| V4 | Evidence persistence | nothing's standing or status changes by evidence alone. VIOLATED if the record says it did |
87	| V5 | Reopening | any reopening of an earlier ruling cites new evidence |
88	| V6 | Authority | the record names the deciding authority (in a "· Governance · X · AUTHORITY" triple or in its text) |
89	| V7 | Supersession | any supersession is explicit and keeps the old record |
90	
91	## E. Rules
92	- Code from the record's text only.
93	- Silence is not evidence: if the record does not say it, the judgement is UNTESTABLE, not VIOLATED.
94	- Do not guess.
95	- Set `authority_named` to true or false.
96	
97	## F. r2 rules (added after Gate 1; they override anything above that is looser)
98	1. **Record-only.**
99	   - Never use knowledge of other records.
100	   - If a guard's satisfaction is not stated in this record, V1 for that act is UNTESTABLE.
101	2. **What counts as an act.** An act is something THIS record itself performs:
102	   - its headline performative; and
103	   - each item it explicitly states as a change it makes ("WHAT IT CHANGES", or an Effect item that is the result of this ruling).
104	
105	   The following are **not** acts:
106	   - state descriptions ("remains", "stays", "is", "still");
107	   - derived consequences ("becomes acceptable", "queue item closed", closure that follows from an acceptance);
108	   - reasons;
109	   - annotations added by *other* rulings. List those under `annotations_by_others`; they are not acts of this record.
110	3. **ADOPT vs ADOPT-DECISION.**
111	   - Code ADOPT only if the record states that the adopted ruling was PREPARED / awaiting adoption.
112	   - Adopting an option, path, review or package content is ADOPT-DECISION.
113	   - If unclear, list both and set V1 AMBIGUOUS.
114	4. **Applicability of V4.** It applies only if the record cites evidence (a finding, counter-evidence, a reproduced result) that bears on an existing decision or standing. Otherwise V4 is UNTESTABLE.
115	5. **Applicability of V5.** It applies only if the record reverses, withdraws, reopens or reclassifies an earlier ruling's decision. Otherwise V5 is UNTESTABLE.
116	6. **Applicability of V7.** It applies only if the record uses a supersession verb, or states that it replaces a named earlier record.
117

ARB Resolution recorded: Tactical DDD commences only after the four business decisions resolve.

44	## DDD-Driven Architectural Implementation Protocol received (17 phases) — ADOPTED AS THE OPERATING STANDARD for implementation work; NOT self-promoted into a standards document
45	
46	**Received from the PA as the going-forward protocol.** In force from the next work package. Its ordering is binding: *Business Model → Strategic Architecture → Architectural Decisions → Approved Design → Implementation → Repository State → Operational Evidence* — never reversed.

50	**Governing principle carried at the top of the protocol** (originating in this slice's mapper self-correction, now generalised by the PA): *a good question does not become a decision by being well argued* → **evidence + reasoning is not authority; a decision is an explicit act by an authority.** Applied twice in WP-2 — the mapper (roadmap won over my simplification argument) and F-T1 (PM-1's wording won over my inference).
51	
52	**GOVERNANCE FLAG — one decision belongs to the DA, not to me.** This protocol is, in substance, the **"Implementation Execution Contract"** candidate that the PA parked on 2026-07-26 with an explicit promotion criterion: *extract only after WP-1 plus a few more slices demonstrate the shape is stable; revisit ~WP-3/WP-4* (recorded with the slice-ledger candidate). Evidence today = **two** slices (WP-1, WP-2). Writing it into a governed standards document now would be exactly what the protocol's own **Phase 16** forbids — *promoting observations into standards* without authorization — so I have **not** created one. Options for the DA: **(a)** adopt now as an explicit early promotion (R-39 is the precedent for DA-authorized early promotion, recorded as an exception so the normal bar stays intact); **(b)** hold to the parked criterion and let WP-3 supply the third instance, following the protocol meanwhile without a standards doc. **Recommendation: (b)** — the protocol is followed either way, and one more slice makes the promotion evidence-backed rather than assertion-backed.
53	
54	*(Practical note: whichever is chosen, the protocol must reach the next session through the runtime path — the WP-3 work plan will carry it, as the WP-1 plan carried the execution contract.)*

57	## X6 2026-07-31 L573
58	
59	### WP-6 FINAL FREEZE VALIDATION — two of my own over-generalizations corrected; framework review ENDS
60	
61	**The ARB caught me generalizing WP-6 observations into framework laws. Both corrections stand.**
62	
63	**1. "Taxonomy determines Authority" was too strong — it is GOVERNANCE-MEDIATED.** The falsifying test is decisive: change governance so integration decisions go to an Architecture Council instead of the ARB, and **the taxonomy is unchanged while the authority changes.** So taxonomy cannot determine authority. Corrected to **"Taxonomy INFORMS Authority; governance rules mediate"**, with the real chain recorded: Finding to Taxonomy to **Governance Rules** to Authority.
64	
65	**DDD justification:** taxonomy is a property of the **finding**; authority is a property of the **organisation deciding about it**. Collapsing them embeds an organisational arrangement into an architectural framework — the same category error N-5 corrected in code, where an orchestrator held a bounded context's meaning.
66	
67	**2. "GREEN = Owner AND Authority AND Artifact" was an equation, and it over-specified.** Those three sufficed *in WP-6* only because Decision C settled the implementation boundary and the ARB settled the scope. **Another slice could have all three and still be blocked** by an unresolved modelling question elsewhere. Corrected to **"GREEN Readiness is derived from the execution dimensions"** — no conjunction asserted. Stating one would generalize a single slice's contingency into a law.
68	
69	**Every dependency is now classified:** the Group-A chain (Taxonomy to Layer to Business Owner to Responsibility Type) and Authority to Artifact are **structural**; Taxonomy to Authority is **governance-derived**; Owner/Authority/Artifact to GREEN is **implementation-derived**. **The single cross-group link is governance-mediated, not structural** — which keeps the taxonomy useful without making it authoritative: it tells you *which governance rule applies*, never *what that rule says*.
70	
71	**What the freeze does NOT freeze: today's governance decisions.** Frozen are dimensions, vocabulary and responsibilities. Values — who the authority is, which artifact is approved, what is in scope — change with governance, and the framework absorbs that without amendment. **A framework that broke under substituting the deciding body would have frozen governance, not structure.**
72	
73	**FRAMEWORK REVIEW ENDS HERE.** Four passes produced N-5, O-1, O-4/O-5 and these two corrections — all from one work package. The next meaningful evidence is **applying it unchanged to independent slices**, not another theoretical improvement. Attention returns to delivery.

78	### WP-6 FRAMEWORK OPERATIONALLY ADOPTED — protocol + template defined; NO framework change
79	
80	**Confirmed first: no framework change is proposed.** The eight dimensions, their vocabulary, their responsibilities and the governance model are untouched. Only *evidence collection* is defined.
81	
82	**Protocol — five steps at each work-package closure:** complete the WP → record **one** of four outcomes → record classification failures → test the reopening criteria → recommend *continue unchanged* or *reopen*.
83	
84	**Four outcomes, closed set:** Exposed a previously unknown defect · Prevented a potential architectural defect · Required no framework changes · **Failed to classify a finding** — the only outcome that can trigger reopening.
85	
86	**One operational clarification added so "exactly one outcome" stays usable:** where several apply, record the **strongest** (Exposed > Prevented > Required no changes), because a framework that exposed a defect trivially also required no changes, and recording the weaker outcome would **hide the stronger evidence**. *Failed to classify* is recorded whenever it occurs regardless. This is a recording convention, **not** a new category.
87	
88	**WP-6's own record opened (outcome deferred to closure, since GREEN and acceptance are pending).** Evidence so far: **N-5** — a *committed* RED test imported a **Domain** exception for an **Application-layer process** rule, exposed by the DDD-layer dimension — plus O-1, O-4, O-5 and S-1..S-3, each a mis-record caught **before** GREEN. **Classification failures: none** — every finding placed in exactly one taxonomy, layer, owner and responsibility type, including the two whose owner is legitimately `UNASSIGNED`. Recommendation: **continue unchanged**.
89	
90	**Independence honoured:** all that evidence was gathered **without** changing a taxonomy, dimension, term or governance rule. *The framework is the measuring instrument, not the subject of measurement.*
91	
92	**Durable home given, no new document created:** the protocol and template live in the plan; a four-line pointer was added to `.claude/MEMORY.md` so future slices find it without re-deriving it — MEMORY.md being the designated place for cross-session conventions.
93	
94	> **The framework is operationally adopted. Future confidence will come from repeated successful application across independent work packages, not from additional theoretical refinement.**
95	
96	
97	## X8 2026-07-31 L3334
98	
99	### 1. "A surviving review is evidence of nothing else" — WITHDRAWN as too absolute
100	**Superseded, retained:** ~~*"A surviving review is evidence that a review happened, and evidence of nothing else."*~~
101	**Operative (Authority formulation):**
102	> **A surviving review IS evidence that the review occurred and records the reasoning applied at that time. It is NOT, by itself, evidence that the reviewed object remains available, or that the review's conclusions remain independently reproducible.**
103	
104	***My version understated the evidentiary value of historical review records — and self-defeatingly so: a surviving review is also evidence of what was reviewed, what was concluded, and what reasoning was recorded, which is precisely why 19 of 21 governing bases could be re-certified at all. The absolute form would have made the IBC-1 re-certification impossible to justify.***
105	
106

## ENTRY ASSESSMENT ACCEPTED (9.9/10) + THE FOUR CONSTITUTIONAL POLICIES RULED — Tactical DDD gate SATISFIED

**Assessment accepted** with two refinements applied first: Collection-consumer finding softened to a current-implementation observation (whether the trust-evidence vocabulary becomes adjudication's canonical evidence source = a Tactical DDD decision, left open); Architectural Risk Register added (R-1..R-7, severity + evidence trace — "the table IS the ARB agenda"). ARB Resolution recorded: Tactical DDD commences only after the four business decisions resolve.

**All four decisions then ruled explicitly (per-item via AskUserQuestion + chair elaborations, recorded at full strength in the assessment's §THE FOUR DECISIONS):**
1. **Superseding Constitutional Publication** — corrections are new publications that supersede, never mutate/reopen, historical publications; Constitutional Publication Invariant recorded; legacy state machine stays isolated from adjudication.
2. **Evidence Preservation Window** — a per-election domain concept (contestation window + max adjudication duration + legal margin); Retention Invariant recorded (evidence for a permissible challenge never expires while the challenge is live); consequence accepted: the Contestation Window must be explicitly defined.
3. **Phase-1 Custodial Constraint** — the codes→votes linkage is intentional, not a defect; three binding invariants (CL-1 custodial-investigation-only · CL-2 privileged + fully audited, every lookup becomes evidence · CL-3 reviewed at Self-Verifying Integrity); binding vocabulary correction: never "the system is anonymous" — *operational ballot secrecy, not cryptographic unlinkability*.
4. **Quarantine Pending Determination** — detection may be automatic, correction may not; Integrity Invariant recorded (automation never determines significance or alters constitutional records); observed connection: the quarantine path is the first natural production entry point for the correction loop's missing head (R-1).

The four rulings form one coherent constitutional policy (recorded); compact binding summary added to `.claude/MEMORY.md`.


## X3 2026-07-26 L94

## ARTIFACT №5 FROZEN · VODP ADOPTED · ARTIFACT №6 (Domain Events) PRODUCED — STOP

**№5 frozen; VODP adopted as permanent governance** (→ MEMORY, with the event companion litmus). **№6 produced: `EPIC-004G_Determination_Domain_Events.md`** — honest shape: the aggregate emits exactly ONE domain event, and its silences (prepare/finalize/refusals emit nothing) are frozen design decisions — the audit defends the deliberate non-events under the entry condition as much as it confirms the event.

**Results:** `DeterminationIssued` CONFIRMED — traces INV-3/4/6/7; special standing recorded: per ADR-T19 Model B it IS the ruling's record (the event and INV-4's fixation are the same fact); strongest removal-test result of the series (removing it silences the entire correction loop). **Three rejections:** DeterminationPrepared (business observes rulings, not drafts) · DeterminationFinalized (no consumer; Round 50-07 confirmed-not-reopened; **reversal condition recorded** — returns via ARB if a finality consumer emerges, e.g. appeal-window closure) · IssuanceRefused (protective refusal to the requester, not a business announcement; the attempted-duplicates observability question noted to audit concerns). **One deferral:** AdjudicationFailureDeclared → the PM design (genuinely business-significant — declare-failure — but the confirmed aggregate doesn't conclude proceedings). **Finding surfaced: the deferrals now visibly cluster around the PM design** (FailureDeclared + EvidenceSet + R-4-expanded seat) — that clustering is itself information for when the PM is designed.


## X4 2026-07-28 L511

## ★ M2 CHECKPOINT DISPOSED — ACCEPT WITH REFINEMENTS (ARB chair, independent review of the actual artifacts) · M3 AUTHORIZED


## X5 2026-07-30 L193

## DDD-Driven Architectural Implementation Protocol received (17 phases) — ADOPTED AS THE OPERATING STANDARD for implementation work; NOT self-promoted into a standards document

**Received from the PA as the going-forward protocol.** In force from the next work package. Its ordering is binding: *Business Model → Strategic Architecture → Architectural Decisions → Approved Design → Implementation → Repository State → Operational Evidence* — never reversed.

**Confirmed already-demonstrated in WP-1/WP-2** (so this formalizes practice rather than introducing untested process): Commission Reset (Ph 1) · Authority Register (Ph 2) · Business Understanding (Ph 3) · Strategic DDD (Ph 4) · Business Model Fidelity (Ph 5) · Traceability (Ph 6) · Simplification (Ph 7) · Business Assumption Review (Ph 8) · RED-first with business-behaviour tests (Ph 10) · minimal GREEN (Ph 11) · Architectural Verification (Ph 13) · Static analysis as design feedback (Ph 14 — the `whereNotIn` type-erasure fix was exactly this) · **Failure Analysis (Ph 15)** — applied when the state guards rejected my own test: the five-way diagnosis returned "incorrect test", so the test changed and the code did not · Governance Discipline (Ph 16) · Completion Review (Ph 17).

**Governing principle carried at the top of the protocol** (originating in this slice's mapper self-correction, now generalised by the PA): *a good question does not become a decision by being well argued* → **evidence + reasoning is not authority; a decision is an explicit act by an authority.** Applied twice in WP-2 — the mapper (roadmap won over my simplification argument) and F-T1 (PM-1's wording won over my inference).

**GOVERNANCE FLAG — one decision belongs to the DA, not to me.** This protocol is, in substance, the **"Implementation Execution Contract"** candidate that the PA parked on 2026-07-26 with an explicit promotion criterion: *extract only after WP-1 plus a few more slices demonstrate the shape is stable; revisit ~WP-3/WP-4* (recorded with the slice-ledger candidate). Evidence today = **two** slices (WP-1, WP-2). Writing it into a governed standards document now would be exactly what the protocol's own **Phase 16** forbids — *promoting observations into standards* without authorization — so I have **not** created one. Options for the DA: **(a)** adopt now as an explicit early promotion (R-39 is the precedent for DA-authorized early promotion, recorded as an exception so the normal bar stays intact); **(b)** hold to the parked criterion and let WP-3 supply the third instance, following the protocol meanwhile without a standards doc. **Recommendation: (b)** — the protocol is followed either way, and one more slice makes the promotion evidence-backed rather than assertion-backed.

*(Practical note: whichever is chosen, the protocol must reach the next session through the runtime path — the WP-3 work plan will carry it, as the WP-1 plan carried the execution contract.)*


## X6 2026-07-31 L573

### WP-6 FINAL FREEZE VALIDATION — two of my own over-generalizations corrected; framework review ENDS

**The ARB caught me generalizing WP-6 observations into framework laws. Both corrections stand.**

**1. "Taxonomy determines Authority" was too strong — it is GOVERNANCE-MEDIATED.** The falsifying test is decisive: change governance so integration decisions go to an Architecture Council instead of the ARB, and **the taxonomy is unchanged while the authority changes.** So taxonomy cannot determine authority. Corrected to **"Taxonomy INFORMS Authority; governance rules mediate"**, with the real chain recorded: Finding to Taxonomy to **Governance Rules** to Authority.

**DDD justification:** taxonomy is a property of the **finding**; authority is a property of the **organisation deciding about it**. Collapsing them embeds an organisational arrangement into an architectural framework — the same category error N-5 corrected in code, where an orchestrator held a bounded context's meaning.

**2. "GREEN = Owner AND Authority AND Artifact" was an equation, and it over-specified.** Those three sufficed *in WP-6* only because Decision C settled the implementation boundary and the ARB settled the scope. **Another slice could have all three and still be blocked** by an unresolved modelling question elsewhere. Corrected to **"GREEN Readiness is derived from the execution dimensions"** — no conjunction asserted. Stating one would generalize a single slice's contingency into a law.

**Every dependency is now classified:** the Group-A chain (Taxonomy to Layer to Business Owner to Responsibility Type) and Authority to Artifact are **structural**; Taxonomy to Authority is **governance-derived**; Owner/Authority/Artifact to GREEN is **implementation-derived**. **The single cross-group link is governance-mediated, not structural** — which keeps the taxonomy useful without making it authoritative: it tells you *which governance rule applies*, never *what that rule says*.

**What the freeze does NOT freeze: today's governance decisions.** Frozen are dimensions, vocabulary and responsibilities. Values — who the authority is, which artifact is approved, what is in scope — change with governance, and the framework absorbs that without amendment. **A framework that broke under substituting the deciding body would have frozen governance, not structure.**

**FRAMEWORK REVIEW ENDS HERE.** Four passes produced N-5, O-1, O-4/O-5 and these two corrections — all from one work package. The next meaningful evidence is **applying it unchanged to independent slices**, not another theoretical improvement. Attention returns to delivery.


## X7 2026-07-31 L611

### WP-6 FRAMEWORK OPERATIONALLY ADOPTED — protocol + template defined; NO framework change

**Confirmed first: no framework change is proposed.** The eight dimensions, their vocabulary, their responsibilities and the governance model are untouched. Only *evidence collection* is defined.

**Protocol — five steps at each work-package closure:** complete the WP → record **one** of four outcomes → record classification failures → test the reopening criteria → recommend *continue unchanged* or *reopen*.

**Four outcomes, closed set:** Exposed a previously unknown defect · Prevented a potential architectural defect · Required no framework changes · **Failed to classify a finding** — the only outcome that can trigger reopening.

**One operational clarification added so "exactly one outcome" stays usable:** where several apply, record the **strongest** (Exposed > Prevented > Required no changes), because a framework that exposed a defect trivially also required no changes, and recording the weaker outcome would **hide the stronger evidence**. *Failed to classify* is recorded whenever it occurs regardless. This is a recording convention, **not** a new category.

**WP-6's own record opened (outcome deferred to closure, since GREEN and acceptance are pending).** Evidence so far: **N-5** — a *committed* RED test imported a **Domain** exception for an **Application-layer process** rule, exposed by the DDD-layer dimension — plus O-1, O-4, O-5 and S-1..S-3, each a mis-record caught **before** GREEN. **Classification failures: none** — every finding placed in exactly one taxonomy, layer, owner and responsibility type, including the two whose owner is legitimately `UNASSIGNED`. Recommendation: **continue unchanged**.

**Independence honoured:** all that evidence was gathered **without** changing a taxonomy, dimension, term or governance rule. *The framework is the measuring instrument, not the subject of measurement.*

**Durable home given, no new document created:** the protocol and template live in the plan; a four-line pointer was added to `.claude/MEMORY.md` so future slices find it without re-deriving it — MEMORY.md being the designated place for cross-session conventions.

> **The framework is operationally adopted. Future confidence will come from repeated successful application across independent work packages, not from additional theoretical refinement.**


## X8 2026-07-31 L3334

### 1. "A surviving review is evidence of nothing else" — WITHDRAWN as too absolute
**Superseded, retained:** ~~*"A surviving review is evidence that a review happened, and evidence of nothing else."*~~
**Operative (Authority formulation):**
> **A surviving review IS evidence that the review occurred and records the reasoning applied at that time. It is NOT, by itself, evidence that the reviewed object remains available, or that the review's conclusions remain independently reproducible.**

***My version understated the evidentiary value of historical review records — and self-defeatingly so: a surviving review is also evidence of what was reviewed, what was concluded, and what reasoning was recorded, which is precisely why 19 of 21 governing bases could be re-certified at all. The absolute form would have made the IBC-1 re-certification impossible to justify.***

# Coding notes

General conventions (apply to all records): V1 is coded UNTESTABLE ("does not apply") when no §C guard is engaged, or when a guard might be engaged but the record doesn't say whether it was satisfied (F1). V6 is coded on the text rather than PRE-R43, because the records are numbered X1–X8, not R-numbers. V6 is coded VIOLATED when no deciding authority is named: V6 tests exactly what the text says, so "silence is not evidence" doesn't turn it into UNTESTABLE.

- X1: V1 is hard. APPROVE/CONFIRM have no guard, but "No-as-health-indicator added" may be new vocabulary (the demonstrated-need bar), and the record doesn't say whether that need was shown. So V1 is UNTESTABLE. "ARB reconfirmed: stop extending" is coded CONFIRM (no change) and not as a new norm.
- X2: The word "supersede" appears only inside the content of Policy 1. The record performs no supersession, so V7 is UNTESTABLE, although a strictly literal reading of F6 would make V7 apply. "Consequence accepted" isn't completed work, so it goes under not_modelled rather than ACCEPT. V2 is SUPPORTED because the gate is recorded as satisfied but Tactical DDD isn't started. I've coded all eight records and saved `CODING.json` (same structure as `FORM.json`) and `NOTES.md` in the bundle directory. I used only `MANUAL.md`, `ROWS.md` and `FORM.json`, and coded each record from its own text.

**Rules I applied across all records** (also stated at the top of `NOTES.md`):
- **V1:** I coded this UNTESTABLE in two cases:
  - no §C guard applies to any of the record's acts;
  - a guard might apply, but the record doesn't say whether it was met (rule F1).
- **V6:** I coded this from the text rather than using PRE-R43, because the records are numbered X1–X8, not R-numbers. Where no deciding authority is named, I coded VIOLATED, since V6 checks exactly what the text says.

**Non-straightforward results by record:**
- **X3 and X7:** V6 is VIOLATED because neither names who decided. In X3 the ARB appears only as the future route for a possible reversal.
- **X4:** This is headline-only. V1 is SUPPORTED because M2 is accepted in the same record that authorizes M3, provided M3 counts as M2's "successor slice".
- **X5:** V1 is AMBIGUOUS. The record declines to promote the protocol into a standards document, citing its own Phase 16 and an earlier promotion criterion. Yet the two slices it cites already meet §C's RAISE bar of at least two instances.
- **X6:** V5 is AMBIGUOUS. It's unclear whether the corrected generalizations were earlier rulings, and the "falsifying test" is a thought-experiment, not new evidence.
- **X8:** V5 and V6 are AMBIGUOUS. "Authority formulation" is only a role label, so `authority_named` is true but V6 is unclear. It's also unclear whether the withdrawn statement was a ruling. V7 is SUPPORTED because the supersession is explicit and the old text is kept, struck through.

**Calls that could reasonably go the other way:**
- **X2:** I left V7 UNTESTABLE because "supersede" appears only inside a policy's content. A strictly literal reading of rule F6 would make V7 apply.
- **X3:** I listed "special standing recorded" under `not_modelled`. If you treat it as a change made by CONFIRM instead, V3 becomes VIOLATED.
- **X6:** I didn't code "corrected" as CORRECT-TEXT, because the record doesn't say it corrects its own text on the same day.
- **X8:** I coded V1 SUPPORTED on the reading that the cited 19-of-21 re-certification counts as "sufficient evidence" for the supersession.

`annotations_by_others` is empty for every record, because none of them contains annotations added by other rulings.
